cards.title: How to read this
items: Solid lines are deployed and verified in dev
Dashed lines and 'planned' tags are designed but not built
Health endpoint returned UP on 14 Nov 2026
AWS details come from the Terraform files and 4 Nov deployment notes, not a live inventory

cards.title: Frontend: rdms-web
items: React 18, Vite, TypeScript, React Router 6, Recharts, d3-geo maps
Roles: Faculty, Top-Level Management, Office of Research (one office per institution)
Seven record types: publications, grants, seed money, FDPs, conferences, honours and awards, intellectual property
Loads one role-scoped data slice, then computes 54 reports, analytics, scores, networks and maps in the browser
Today it runs on its own Node/Express + SQLite prototype server; src/lib/store.ts is the only seam to replace
Decided host: Hostinger at dev-unirise.mentoredge.co.in, manual upload of dist/

cards.title: unirise-api: built
items: Spring Boot 4.1.2 (webmvc, security, validation, actuator), Java 21, Maven, JdbcClient, no JPA
Tenancy: TenantRoutingDataSource, TenantDirectory, Provisioner, Migrator, TenantLifecycle; LRU pools (5 connections per tenant, 50 open pools)
Flyway run in code: control V1-V4 at start, tenant V1-V5 by the migrator
Platform API (X-Admin-Key): create, list, suspend, export, delete tenants; migrations; usage
Entries: publications, grants, seed money with draft, submit, review (EntryWorkflow)
Also built with no screen: org tree, role grants, milestones, meeting logs, projects, periods, CSV import (parked)
19 SQL reports with CSV export; 36 tests on real PostgreSQL 16 via Testcontainers

cards.title: unirise-api: planned
items: Three-role AccessService; only the Office of Research reviews
Email + password sign-in: cookie session, CSRF header, lockout, idle timeouts (OIDC later)
New tables: fdp, conference, honour, intellectual_property, biodata, profile_change, notice
Under Review status, display codes (PUB, GRT, ...), grant outcome endpoint
Office approvals queue, user management, settings, notices, admin action log
Per institution: feature switches, custom fields (JSONB), configurable option lists
Scoped data-slice endpoint so reports stay computed in the browser

cards.title: Data
items: One PostgreSQL 16 RDS instance: db.t4g.micro, 20 GB gp3, encrypted, private, 7-day backups, no Multi-AZ
Control plane: institution, institution_credential, institution_secret, user_token, migration_run, usage_counter, platform_access_log
Each tenant database: institution, researcher, org_unit (+closure), appointment, app_user, role_grant, relationship, access_log
Entries: publication (+author), research_grant (+investigator), seed_window, seed_proposal (+investigator), review_event
Other: tenant_settings, milestone, meeting_log, project (+member), period, period_snapshot
The tenant is chosen from the credential only, never from the request

cards.title: Security and network
items: API accepts :8080 only from the load balancer's security group
RDS accepts :5432 only from the API and DB admin task security groups
No NAT, bastion, EC2 or paid interface endpoints; tasks use public IPs for outbound HTTPS; free S3 gateway endpoint
CORS allows only https://dev-unirise.mentoredge.co.in on /api/**
Today: X-API-Key per tenant, X-Admin-Key for operators, invitation token to bearer session
Only the admin task's execution role can read the RDS master secret
Still a shortcut: tenant DB passwords sit in a control-plane table; move to Secrets Manager before real data

cards.title: Operations
items: DNS in Hostinger: CNAME api.dev-unirise.mentoredge.co.in to the load balancer
CI (GitHub Actions): mvnw verify and docker build; no deploy step
Deploy by hand: scripts/push-image.sh, then tofu apply with the pinned image digest
scripts/run-db-admin.sh bootstrap | backup-restore <tenant>; restore drill passed 4 Nov
OpenTofu state in an encrypted S3 bucket; 71 managed resources
Estimated cost: $50 to $70 a month before tax and usage
Not started: deploy pipeline, scheduled backups, alarms, IAM users with MFA, budget alerts, SES production access, production environment
